note: family-architecture.md 5.0a. DATA per-tier here; CHECKER is the shared harness/divergence_register.py; PROBE is per-tier and named above because it must speak this tier's language. sv-div-1 and the retired sv-div-2 are KIND=provenance: the model and the simulator have not been shown to disagree -- what outran the evidence is the CLAIM of agreement. sv-div-3 (2026-10-28) was the tier's first KIND=semantic row: the model and IEEE 1800-2023 (with Icarus) DID disagree, by decision; it RETIRED the same day by REFUSAL (WP4: self-reading always_comb bodies are refused at instantiation, LeanModels/Sv/CombGuard2.lean), a third way out beside re-running and remodelling. Provenance retires by re-running; semantic retires by remodelling. RETIREMENT: sv-div-2 retired 2026-08-24 and moved to retired_rows. Its two guards were deleted from the probe in that same commit and were RESTORED on 2026-08-25 under 5.0a clause 3: retirement moves a row to the archive, it does not end the watch, so a retired row keeps naming two guards and the checker verifies they EXIST. A retired still_divergent is expected to report not-held; the probe reports it and excludes it from the exit code. Kept rather than dropped so the register can be AGED -- a debt that was paid is evidence, and a ledger that forgets its closed rows cannot show that any row ever closes.

retired_rows.born_with_retirement_in_flight: This row is filed with its remedy already scheduled -- the rewording is batched into the next tier-Sv tenure alongside slotStep's first piece, since these are files inside the build glob and docs-class cannot carry them. It is registered anyway rather than left as an in-flight intention, because this lane RECORDED the audit disposition as 'ACCEPTED, rewording' on 2026-08-23 and then did not apply it, and the gap survived two green landings. Recording an acceptance is not making the change; a row that ages is what makes the difference visible.
retired_rows.retired_by: All 10 sites reworded from 'reproduces the Xcelium-verified outcomes' to 'consistent with the LRM rules the differential harness verified', each stating plainly that the guarded stimuli were not themselves simulated and that harness/sv/cases.json drives different vectors. sv_div_2_still_divergent counted the surviving sites to ZERO, which is what closed the row -- the count closed it, not an assertion that it was fixed. Its two guards were deleted in the same commit as the row, on the reading that a guard whose row is gone guards nothing. 5.0a clause 3 (2026-08-25) reversed that reading and the guards were restored: a row whose guard is gone is unfalsifiable in BOTH directions, so the archive keeps the watch that would notice the divergence coming back.

retired_rows.site: LeanModels/Sv/Sem2.lean `combSettle2`: the comb settle loop re-runs an always_comb process until no signal changes. Divergent on a body that reads a variable it also writes, before or without writing it on the executed path. Spelling: `always_comb begin if (c) t = a; y = t; t = b; end` (Examples/system-verilog/sem2/rbw_held) and `always_comb begin y = t; t = a; end` (sem2/rbw_comb). Reachable through `run2` and every `name.sem` from `load_design_sv2`; NOT through the always_comb settle-theorem API, whose lowering refuses such bodies (`SymState.selfReadFree`; `rbw_refused`, `held_refused` in LeanModels/Sv/Comb2ProcExample.lean).
retired_rows.oracle: IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2.1: an always_comb block runs once at time zero and then once per change of a variable in its implicit sensitivity list, which EXCLUDES every variable the block writes; the block is never woken by its own write of t, so y shows the value t had when the block last ran. Icarus 12.0 gives y = 01 01 11 on rbw_held's pinned stimulus (c=0 a=00 b=01; c=0 a=00 b=10; c=1 a=11 b=10) and y = 00 00 01 10 on rbw_comb's (a = 00 01 10 11). MEASURED by the probe on every run: sv_div_3_still_divergent drives Icarus on the committed SV with the stimulus read from the model's own pin, through harness/sv/gen_tb2.py. Yosys 0.53 proc does NOT give this answer: it synthesizes the settle answer, so simulation and synthesis split on this shape.
retired_rows.model: run2 settles the body to its fixpoint: y = c ? a : b on rbw_held (01 10 11) and y = a on rbw_comb (00 01 10 11). MEASURED BY THE BUILD in the layered shape of family-architecture 5.0a (b): LeanModels/Sv/Comb2ProcExample.lean `#guard (run2 heldDesign ...) == some ["01", "10", "11"]` and its rbwDesign twin, tied to the committed SV sources by each fixture's agree.lean (`rbw_held.sem` has heldDesign's declarations and prints heldDesign's processes). The probe verifies those pins EXIST, outside comments, and reads their stimulus and expected traces; it runs no Lean.
retired_rows.inherited_note: ORIGINATED here. combSettle2's fixpoint settle is this lane's own decision for combinational processes, and the divergence was found by the lane's own review of the always_comb settle theorem (docs/sv-charter.md, '`always_comb` in the comb settle theorem -- 2026-10-27', review fix), which narrowed the proof API and left run2 as it was.
retired_rows.retirement_condition: Sem2 runs an always_comb block as IEEE 1800-2023 9.2.2.2.1 does -- once per wake-up, never re-triggered by its own writes -- so the build-pinned run2 traces become Icarus's (01 01 11 and 00 00 01 10) and sv_div_3_still_divergent stops holding. The guard drives Icarus with the model pin's own stimulus, so the row retires by the behaviour changing and cannot be closed by assertion. MUST NOT MOVE: every always_comb body the settle-theorem profile accepts keeps a single run equal to its fixpoint (runCombProcess2_alwaysComb_idem), and the differential rows fa_comb_proc, mux4_case, onehot_dec, latch_comb and addsub_comb* stay PASS; a remodel that changes an accepted body's answer has fixed the wrong thing.
retired_rows.why_kept: Lead decision, 2026-10-28: Sem2 stays as it is. On this shape run2 agrees with the hardware Yosys synthesizes, which is what svGolf scores, so a post-synthesis simulation check cannot see the difference; remodelling would put run2 at odds with the netlist on every self-reading body. sv_div_3_has_not_widened measures that agreement (Yosys 0.53 prep; eval on all 32 two-state input points of rbw_held and all 4 of rbw_comb), so the reason for carrying the debt is gated together with the debt.
retired_rows.widening_measured: sv_div_3_has_not_widened holds only while (1) the build-pinned run2 trace is the declared settle answer and Yosys gives the settle answer on every two-state point; (2) Icarus gives exactly the declared stale trace: it differs from run2 only where t is read stale (rbw_held cycle 1, rbw_comb cycles 1-3) and agrees on rbw_held's c = 1 cycle, whose executed path writes t before reading it, and on cycle 0, where the time-zero run and the first stimulus both wake the block -- runs that agree exhibit the window's edge; (3) rbw_refused / held_refused and the agree.lean `lowerComb.isNone` guards are still declared, so nothing about these bodies is proved through the settle-theorem API.
retired_rows.rejected_alternative: Refusing self-reading always_comb bodies at ingestion, as the lane does where the tools split with each other (docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md, 'Refused where the oracles split'). Not taken: under 5.0a a refusal adopted to avoid a debt is a weakening wearing a boundary's clothes; the model answers, matches the scored hardware, and its difference from the standard is registered instead.
retired_rows.gated: While this row is live no claim in this tier may describe run2's always_comb as the IEEE event semantics, or a theorem about a self-reading always_comb proved through name.sem as simulator-validated. Such a design is correct for its synthesized netlist and differs from every IEEE-conforming simulator.
retired_rows.retired_by: REFUSAL, by decision (Thomas, 2026-10-28, WP4 of the svGolf round 3): no answer is safe on a self-reading always_comb -- Icarus 12, Xcelium 24.03/26.09 and mox-sim give the stale value, Verilator 5.042, Yosys 0.53 and the settle semantics the combinational one -- so the model stops answering. The always_comb self-read guard (LeanModels/Sv/CombGuard2.lean, `Stmt2.combViol`/`combGuardProc`) is applied in `instProcess2` (LeanModels/Sv/Param2.lean) at every parameter point: a body that, on some control path, reads a bit before the path writes it and writes that bit later becomes the loud `AlwaysComb:self-read` process, so no `name.sem` (flat, hierarchical, generate-expanded) and no differential-runner design runs it, and `load_design_sv2` refuses the envelope at the defaults with the same message. The rule is per bit and path-sensitive: latches, and latches that read their held value, stay admitted (one run is the fixpoint there), and CombGuard2Sound.lean proves that every admitted body is idempotent on shaped states (`runCombProcess2_alwaysComb_idem_of_admits`), i.e. the settle semantics and one run per wake-up agree on it. The fixtures rbw_comb and rbw_held are now refusal fixtures (their agree.lean pins load_design_sv2's refusal text with #guard_msgs and checks that the instantiation is the hand-built design's declarations with the guard's refusal of its body), and harness/sv/cases2.json carries their loud-refusal rows plus seven more refused shapes (rbw_bits, rbw_cond, rbw_case_item, rbw_dyn, rbw_part, rbw_nested; rbw_compound is refused earlier by the extractor) and nine admitted ones (acg_*), each admitted row PASS against Icarus 12. The retirement condition as written (Sem2 remodelled to the event semantics) did NOT occur: Sem2 is unchanged, and the hand-built heldDesign/rbwDesign pins in Comb2ProcExample still give the settle answer. The divergence is closed by making it unreachable from ingested designs, which is a narrowing of the tier, recorded as such. Guards change meaning as 5.0a clause 3 asks: sv_div_3_still_divergent now holds (the ALARM) only when a refusal pin is gone -- the instProcess2 hook, an agree.lean refusal pin or instantiation link, a cases2.json refusal row, rbw_guard/held_guard -- and sv_div_3_has_not_widened keeps measuring the tool split that justifies the refusal (hand-built run2 pins = settle, Icarus = declared stale trace, Yosys = settle on every two-state point).
